description: Discover what is possible here: shared tools, models, availability and known failures, from the same catalogue the user sees. Use it for questions like what cool things can we do, ideas for this specimen, what should we try next, or whether you can do something; also consult it when unsure of a capability. Turn the catalogue into a few concrete, varied possibilities grounded in the current specimen, selected subject, existing results and the user's interests. Explain what each would reveal or let them explore. Combine available capabilities creatively, such as measurement with comparison or a reference beside a magnification; do not just recite tool or model names. Distinguish something usable now from something needing setup or known to be broken. Availability does not guarantee a scientific result or a successful external lookup. Mention models when that helps the choice; with operation, inspect which models can do it here. Quick actions can be yours; sustained investigations can go to researchers while conversation continues. Asking for ideas does not itself request running them. This lookup runs no analysis and starts no researcher.
name: capabilities

description: Open an independent live magnifier on an object, retaining other windows, or change how close an already open one looks. Each object gets its own window. level: "fit" (the whole object filling the window: what "show it up close", "in HD" and "the whole cell" mean; a small thing is then already enlarged past the camera's detail, and the answer says so), a number (×N closer than fit, e.g. 4), "more" (twice as close), "less" (half), or "max" (the closest it goes, only when asked for the closest). Any level works and it never refuses: past the camera's resolution the picture is pixel-enlarged (blocky, no new detail). Without object it acts on the open magnifier. This changes camera magnification, never an image source’s size. hold=true shows the sharpest recent frame instead of the moving live view. picture names an existing image URL from the view notes to show beside the camera crop; use it when a specific reference or snapshot is requested. Without picture, beside=true keeps the picture in the magnifier (a reference photo, a researcher's picture) and shows the object's live close-up next to it, both at once in the one window ("a magnification next to the photo").
name: zoom

beside.description: next to the current picture in the magnifier

description: Switch the open magnifier to one of its existing sources, without changing zoom or losing the other sources. source is a key from the current magnifier sources in your view notes: live, held, or an existing picture URL. Selecting a picture shows that entire image, including all subjects already in it; selecting live or held restores any camera comparison. Optional beside: another existing picture URL to show alongside this source, or an empty string to hide the separate peer pane while retaining it. Does not fetch or generate a new picture or change what an existing picture depicts. If the wanted subject is a saved member, use present(what=cN, do=open) to open its original crop without a live outline. Returns the actual selected source for the answer to use.

description: Retrieve a real photo directly into its own window, usually within seconds: a reference photo with its source and available attribution, not this slide ("show me a real picture of a stoma", "what does a normal one look like?"). Not an AI illustration, and no research report. Uses Gemini 3.8 Flash with Google Search across the public web, without domain restrictions. A failed lookup does not require a researcher. Preserve the current request's imaging method, magnification and subject in subject and search_terms; do not inherit old university, collection or domain restrictions from earlier requests unless the user retains them. omit search_terms when the full request is already concise. Never drop a required detail just to get a match. show=false fetches and retains without changing the current magnifier or motion view; its source output 0 lets a later step use present do=open source={step:N,output:0} for this step N, without predicting an ID. Alternatively use the returned resource's exact day/id, version=null and picture=0 to open an independent window. Every photo found is looked at, its pixels against the whole request (subject, how many, kind of view, imaging, a different one from those already in this Project); one that fails is never returned, and the receipt says what the returned photo shows from that look: describe the photo only in those words, never as what was asked. description is an optional note on the topic, kept as a note, never as what the photo shows. Default/show=true opens its independent window, retaining the magnification and other work. In a native workspace, with default show=true, beside=true fits the new photo beside the original requesting browser's pointed window (or its sole visible window) before its first paint, leaving that anchor fixed; ambiguity or no room is reported. For an explicit anchor, use show=false then present(do=open,source={step:N,output:0}, relation={kind:beside,reference:{instanceId:the exact observed window ID}}) for initial fitting. Arranging an already-open window preserves its current size and may not fit. n: another match (2, 3...) when asked for another or a different one; photos already kept in this Project are then never returned.
name: reference_photo

beside.description: with default show=true, initial fit beside the original requesting browser's pointed or sole visible window, before first paint; anchor unchanged. show=false only retains; choose an exact anchor with present open+relation

description: Start a researcher for sustained investigation, comparison across sequences, independent confirmation, or producing a requested report, illustration, video or lesson while conversation continues. For retrieving a photo or existing work use reference_photo or show_result directly; a failed lookup does not itself call for a report. Use your own tools for ordinary live questions and actions. One request starts one researcher; when the user asks for more than one, list each start in the same answer. When the user's words add to or change what they just asked a researcher for (Researchers lists it just started: queued, starting or running, from their previous words), pass them to that one with researcher_note instead of starting another; start a new one when they ask for another researcher or separate work. effort: instant (about 15 s and 3 model rounds before it is told to write up); quick (about 75 s and 8 model rounds before it is told to write up); standard (about 360 s and 16 model rounds before it is told to write up); deep (about 1080 s and 32 model rounds before it is told to write up). No clock cuts its work off (it is told to write up, and asks the user before going past an hour), but choose the effort that fits the work: the app's operations take about 5-7 s for one motion measurement, about 10 s to segment a view and a model round 10-30 s, plus the write-up of everything it read. Quick fits a lookup or one or two measurements; several measurements with a comparison or average need standard. Deep requires an explicit request for thorough/deep research. For an explicitly requested handoff, inputs names exact earlier step outputs: wait for those original runs, then use only their completed inputs. deliverable: research (default; from quick up it can chart or animate a saved table such as the measurements, drawn from the table's own values), annotated_image (labels on the object's photo), image (an AI illustration, never a real photo: for a real photo use reference_photo), report, video (an AI-generated video from the photo, never of data) or lesson (only when the user explicitly asks for one). Honor the user's effort limit: never increase it to fit a format. Video needs standard or deep, a lesson quick or more; image/annotated_image need quick or above. For a quick explanation or teaching, use research: it can explain in writing without a full lesson. If the requested format cannot fit, explain that before starting. From quick effort up it can have the app run saved scientific workflows, segment every cell, make a clearer picture, measure saved labels or measure what moves for its own reading (an instant one cannot); whatever else the app does, run it yourself with your own tool, the first time.
name: start_researcher

description: Find and outline things by name or by how they look, in the view or inside an outlined object ("the nucleus inside that cell", "every red cell", "point out the pore in the stoma"). Use it whenever the user asks to point out, find or show a part inside an outlined object (zoom only magnifies; it outlines nothing). Inside an object it looks at a close-up of it and keeps that object by default. Set keep_container=false when the user wants only the found part, replacing its prior app-drawn containing outline after finding it; user-drawn outlines always stay. An inside=sN search uses that seen region without outlining its container. all=true outlines every one; all=false selects one; omit all to follow the quantity in the user's request. like=<an outline> outlines every thing that looks like it; keep=true keeps your earlier highlights. by="cells": a cell finder outlines every cell and you pick which are the ones asked for; best for many cells of a smear or tissue (red or white blood cells, cheek cells), not for tiny things like platelets or bacteria (blood smear bench: every red cell 0.90 found this way against 0.60 by looking). It sees the camera's picture only, never the outlines the app draws (by their colour: highlight where).

With id and inspect=true, attach that saved picture to the next answer for visual questions; captions alone are not pixels. At most two pictures per request. Nothing given, the summary ("what data do we have?"); kind or query, those; id, one in full: an entry, a saved member (c17) or an outline (o3). description: Make a clearer picture of the view from real camera frames and show it in the magnifier. how: "average" (the default) averages the still frames of the last second or so, aligned, for less noise and grain; "sharpest" picks the sharpest recent frame; "stack" focus-stacks the frames from the last turn of the focus knob, each place taken from the frame where it was sharpest, so more of a thick specimen is in focus at once. Use it when the user asks to clean up, sharpen or enhance the picture, reduce the noise, or stack the focus. Nothing is invented: every pixel comes from the camera. object: zoom the result to that outline.

Use it when the user asks to take a picture, save or keep the view, or a snapshot. It is of the window the user was looking at when they asked (a live close-up: what it showed, on the frame of that moment), or of the object named, else of the view; it opens beside that window and is kept by its own id (open that id again when they cannot see it, never take another). For a clean, unannotated camera picture use overlays=false: no masks, labels, scale bar or footer; provenance stays with the saved file. labels=false alone leaves only the labels off.

object.description: object id, "target N", or a label

description: Present layers, document windows and the magnifier. do=place with placement puts a thing where it is asked (overlay on the live view, beside, new-tab, window, replace, close, only), done once the screen shows it. Choose an operation supported by the exact target. Document windows (notes, masks, tables) close without removing Data. Outlines are named or segmented specimen shapes; they are distinct from population masks and motion trajectory layers. A prior step N that made motion tracks or a population can be addressed with what='@N' for layer show/hide/opacity; never predict its new ID. Reopen saved work by its exact ID from resources, without rerunning its maker: open shows it in the reader; show draws a layer on the picture. Open a saved member (c17) for its original clean crop without making a live outline. Historical motion tracks need verified field placement; current-camera trails draw only on their exact paired camera frame and include camera/stage motion. For moving motion into a corner, open its existing source in a native window, then resize/move and fade that window; hide its tracks layer if transferring it off the camera. The measurement is unchanged. Restore the overlay with show on tracks:mN. Changing layer opacity alone does not move it.

description: List the Tabs inside this Project (a Tab arranges this Project’s windows; a new Project is new_project), what each holds and what is in front, or explicitly create, rename, switch, add a retained resource, move a placement, arrange, keep only one thing, or close a named Tab. Each item has a kind (table, outlines, tracks, image, reference, document, graph, video, web-page, magnifier, note); list with kind=table gives only the Tabs holding a table: "which Tab has the measurements?" is answered from kinds, never titles. Researcher Tabs list what they show. Placing on a Tab: arrange puts its windows and the live view side by side (beside); only keeps just `keep` (window or placement ids) open there, closing the rest and hiding the specimen (Main’s floats small); both done once the screen shows it. Closing hides an arrangement and never deletes Data. Each Tab also holds the specimen, the live view: it fills the Tab behind its windows, floats as a small window (a new Tab opens with it so), or is hidden there; list and the screen say which. It counts in what a Tab shows: name it when it is there, and float or hide it too for only one thing open in a Tab or everything else closed (action specimen with specimen fill, float or hide; Main’s floats, never hides; done once the screen shows it). Mutations require the user’s request. Always name tab by its exact ID from list; move also needs from and placement. No implicit active Tab or other Studio fallback. Completion is acknowledged by the originating Studio after its arrangement save; visibility is reported separately. A measurements table in a Tab (new or not) is show_measurements with tab: one action, confirmed on screen.

It opens in its own sandboxed window with its source and link shown; placement: window (the default, in front), beside, new-tab, only or replace. Done once the screen shows it.
